As for the ascription of this addition to our master al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, the blessings of God be upon him — while the Twelver Shia, despite their disagreement with him in school, nonetheless employ this sentence in the call to prayer — it is a plainly void ascription, and whoever makes it speaks in raving slander.

As for his saying that ascribing this subtraction to Umar ibn al-Khattab is unacceptable because it does not exist in the books of those people: his saying carries no weight. Regarding the books that those people rely on for soundness — such as Sahih al-Bukhari and the rest of the five and al-Mishkat — the disagreement of their own scholars over those books' soundness, and the fabricated reports found within them, relieve the people of truth of any need to refute them or to set up proofs against them. Moreover, the narration transmitted by our master al-Qadi al-Numan from our master Jafar al-Sadiq predates the compilation of those people's books; and it may well be that when they saw in it an opening for censure against them, they dropped it and erased it, fearing to give room to the censure of the people of truth — for such has been their custom. This is the refutation of the saying that one who adds to the call to prayer is like one who subtracts from it.

As for the origin of the ascription of this addition, the answer is that this phrase and the testimony to guardianship issued from the Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib, concerning himself, when the office of guardianship passed to him after the Prophet — just as the Prophet testified for himself to prophethood and messengership, and as God, glorified is He, testified concerning His own essence, saying:

> شَهِدَ اللهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ

And that was after the verse of guardianship was revealed concerning him — His saying, "Your guardian is only God and His Messenger," to the end of it. Though they have disagreed about the occasion of its revelation, out of a desire on their part to deny his guardianship, their books are nonetheless filled with testimony that it was revealed concerning the Commander of the Believers, the blessings of God be upon him. In this there is sufficiency for those who seek right direction and guidance; and as for the stubborn disputer, he has nothing but going astray.

> وَكُلُّ إِنَاءٍ يَتَرَشَّحُ بِمَا فِيهِ وَاللهُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ

Every vessel seeps with what is in it, and God guides whom He wills to a straight path.

edits.chapter_key: where a muslim stands to pray
edits.body_md:
In the book of questions and answers I mentioned at the outset — arranged by one of its compilers in the order of the chapters of *Daaim al-Islam* — I find the matter of mosques treated as follows.

**Question:** What do you say concerning what has come in the Sharia forbidding prayer between graves, the dislike of building a mosque beside them, and the saying of the Messenger of God (ع):

> جُعِلَتْ لِي الْأَرْضُ مَسْجِدًا وَطَهُورًا إِلَّا الْحَمَّامَ وَالْمَقْبَرَةَ وَالْحُشَّ

The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, except for the bathhouse, the cemetery, and the latrine.

Explain its detail to us. **Answer:** This is in accordance with what has been stated in the outward sense of the Sharia. One does not pray in any of those places at all, and no mosque is built beside graves.

**Question:** What do you say concerning a mosque given over to public use that stands above a house or a shop: may its owners remove it and pull it down, or not? **Answer:** If it belongs to him alone and he has not given it over to public use, he may pull it down. If it has been given over to public use, it is not lawful for him to pull it down; and if it collapses on its own, nothing is owed by him.

**Question:** What do you say concerning a man who wishes to build the congregational mosque or another on his own property: must he seek the governor's permission for that, or not? **Answer:** He does as he wishes and does not seek permission.

**Question:** What do you say concerning what has come in the Book of Purity — that there is no prayer for the neighbor of the mosque except in the mosque, meaning that his prayer does not carry the merit of one who prays in the mosque — and also that the prayer of a man alone in his house is a single prayer? So, our master, what is the difference between the neighbor of the mosque and any other person, if the prayer of a man in his house is a single prayer? **Answer:** The neighbor of the mosque is the one who hears the call to prayer, and the prayer of a man without congregation is a single prayer. For the neighbor of the mosque, however, it is disliked for him to pray alone in his house without an excuse.

**Question:** What do you say concerning what is related in the Book of Purity — that when the mosque of the Prophet (ع) leaked, the people said, "O Messenger of God, if only we plastered it," and he said:

> لَا، عَرِيشٌ كَعَرِيشِ مُوسَىٰ

No; a shelter like the shelter of Moses.

What is the meaning of this saying? **Answer:** It means that this is not like the plastered shelter of Moses.

**Question:** What do you say concerning a man who hears the call to prayer from a mosque in which one of the licensed men of the mission leads the prayer, while the hearer prays in his house with another licensed man: have the two of them forfeited a prayer of merit, or not? **Answer:** The prayer in the mosque is more excellent, as the Prophet (ع) said:

> لَا صَلَاةَ لِجَارِ الْمَسْجِدِ إِلَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ

There is no prayer for the neighbor of the mosque except in the mosque.

**Question:** What do you say concerning a mosque in which the imam leads the noon prayer with the congregation, while another imam leads that same prayer with another congregation on the roof: is that permissible, and is the prayer of greeting prayed both below and above, or not? **Answer:** There is no harm in it, and there is no prayer of greeting above it for one who has already prayed it below.

**Question:** What do you say concerning a quarter in which there are several mosques, and a man leaves his house at the time of prayer: may he pass by the nearer mosque and go to the farther one because the licensed man in the farther one is of greater rank than the licensed man of the nearer? **Answer:** Yes, that is established, and there is no blame upon one who does so.

**Question:** What does our master say concerning a mosque that a man sets up within his house but has not dedicated to God, exalted be He, as a place open to the people: may he relocate it or absorb it into an enlargement of his house, and is the prayer of greeting prayed in it, or not? **Answer:** If the mosque is open to the people, the prayer of greeting is prayed in it. If it is confined within the house and has not been made open, it is a place of prayer only — the prayer of greeting is not prayed in it, and he may incorporate it into whatever part of the house he wishes, as long as he has not made it open.

**Question:** What does our master say concerning a man who comes to the mosque at the time of dawn while the imam is praying the obligatory prayer in congregation, and the one arriving is able to pray the Sunnah and still join the imam: does he pray the greeting and the Sunnah, or does he enter with the imam? **Answer:** If it is possible for him to reach the prayer before the imam bows, let him pray whatever he wishes of the Sunnah prayers before the imam raises his head from bowing.

**Question:** What does our master say concerning a man who comes to the mosque before midday to make up an obligatory prayer he has missed: does he pray the greeting, or not? **Answer:** He does not pray a Sunnah prayer while an obligatory prayer is owed by him, except the Sunnah of the dawn, for that has been joined to the obligatory prayers; and the greeting is not prayed except at times when the Sunnah prayer is permitted.

**Question:** What does our master say concerning one who comes while the imam is in the obligatory dawn prayer and enters into it with him: does he make up the greeting or the Sunnah after finishing it, or after midday? **Answer:** If he prays anything before the greeting, its time has passed. There is no harm in making up the Sunnah after the obligatory dawn prayer, as long as the sun has not yet risen — or after midday, or at night.

**Question:** What does our master say concerning an imam who has led the congregation in prayer in a mosque and then departed, after which another licensed man comes: does he lead that same prayer in congregation in that mosque, or not? **Answer:** Two imams do not lead prayer at one time in one assembly, unless the imam is overtaken by something that breaks his state and he appoints another imam in his place.

**Question:** If the imam leads the funeral prayer with the people in the mosque, what is the ruling regarding the greeting? **Answer:** If they entered the mosque at a time when supererogatory prayers are permitted, they pray the greeting first.

Other rulings follow:

- Whoever prays in open country and finds nothing to set up as a screen draws a line and prays; he does not leave his sandal facing the qibla as a screen.
- Whoever prays the doubled prayer or the Sunnah of noon in his house and then comes to the mosque begins with the greeting of the mosque, if his entry is at the time of noon or when dawn has broken.
- Whoever builds a mosque and people are buried around it afterward, prayer in it is permitted; but if it was built after the grave, prayer in it is not permitted.
- It is disliked that the qibla of the mosque face toward a bathhouse, toward graves, or toward a latrine.
- Whoever does not know the qibla because something prevents him exerts his judgment and prays. If he errs and learns of the error while he is still in the prayer and the time is short, he turns toward the direction of the House and completes his prayer, provided he was between the east and the west; but if he had his back to the Kaaba, nothing suffices him but repetition.
- If two directions are confused for a man — so that he sees the qibla as lying in each of them and neither of the two prevails in his judgment — he prays toward both directions together; and the like of this has been mentioned concerning the four directions.
- Whoever travels and the time of prayer comes upon him on the road while he is in a state of major impurity and finds no water, and there is a mosque on the way, performs the dry ablution and prays in the mosque.
- If prayer has been performed in congregation in the mosque and the imam departs and the congregation departs, and a second imam comes with a congregation, that imam prays by himself and they pray by themselves. The leading of prayer is not held in one mosque more than once.
- Whoever enters the mosque, prays the greeting of the mosque, then goes out for a need and returns, prays the greeting of the mosque again.
- A man does not pray with camels facing the qibla; but if they are cattle, sheep, or the like, the prayer is permitted.
- Whoever prays the doubled prayer in his house in its proper time and then enters the mosque may not pray the greeting of the mosque until dawn breaks; then he begins with the greeting of the mosque and prays the dawn prayer. If he enters the mosque and prays the greeting of the mosque and the time of the doubled prayer returns, he repeats the doubled prayer, for there is no prayer between the doubled prayer and the dawn prayer.
- Whoever prays the obligatory prayer in the mosque, and another comes and places a sword facing the qibla, and the worshipper is under a restriction and unable to move away, completes the prayer, and his prayer is valid.
- It is disliked to pray between the two pillars as long as the worshipper finds another place in the mosque; and if he finds none, the prayer is permitted.
- If land lies between partners and one of them builds a mosque upon it, prayer in it is permitted, because he built on his own property; and if the other builds a mosque, prayer in it is permitted also.

From the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: It is disliked that the qibla of the mosque face toward a bathhouse, toward graves, or toward a latrine. Whoever does not know the qibla because something prevents him exerts his judgment and prays; if he errs and learns of the error while he is still in the prayer and the time is short, he turns toward the direction of the House and completes his prayer, if it was between the east and the west; but if he had his back to the Kaaba, nothing suffices him but repetition. And if two directions are confused for a man — so that he sees the qibla as lying in each of them and neither of the two prevails in his judgment — he prays toward both directions together; and the like of this has been mentioned concerning the four directions.

From the book *Tawil al-Daaim*: as for His saying, وسلاحكم, the laying down of weapons and the bringing of them into the mosques is not permitted in the outward sense, except for the imam of the mosque on the day of Friday.

It is said in the book *al-Idah* that Abu Abd Allah (ع) disliked that a mosque be inside a house with a door locked upon it.

It is said in *Majalis al-Bayan* that prayer is disliked in twelve places:

1. The cemetery
2. The slaughterhouse
3. The bathhouse
4. The latrine
5. The resting places of camels
6. Prayer facing a sleeping person
7. Prayer without a screen
8. Upon wet, impure ground
9. Upon anything of food
10. Prayer in places of worship
11. Churches
12. The houses of the Magians, unless they have been sprinkled with water

Our master and our lord and our father, Muhammad ibn al-Fahd — may God exalt his sanctity and grant us his intercession and his company — said in his noble epistle, which he named *The Clear Highway of the Path of Guidance for Those Who Seek Guidance, and the Uncoverer of Obscurities in the Juristic Questions of Religion*:

**Question Nineteen:** You asked also — may God, glorified be He, grant you success in what pleases Him — about prayer in a domed structure or a mosque in which there is a grave on any of its sides. **Answer:** You have, in this too, by the granting of success from God, glorified be He, the sound word concerning it, and its truth is this: if the said domed structure or the said mosque was built for prayer to be performed in it, and afterward the making of a grave in it occurred to one who made it there and buried a dead person in it after that, then prayer in either of them is permitted, in its obligatory prayers and its Sunnah prayers. But if either of them was built on account of a grave that required it, coming after the grave, then their ruling is the ruling of the cemetery, and prayer is never permitted in either of them for one who would pray.

He said also — may God exalt his sanctity — in the noble epistle mentioned, concerning the matter of the greeting of the mosque built for the seeking of the face of its Owner:

You also asked — may God, glorified be He, grant you success in all that pleases Him — about the prayer of greeting the mosque: is it obligatory only within the mosque itself, never in its courtyard and forecourt? And if someone enters the mosque and performs it there, then goes out to the courtyard and returns, is he obliged to perform it again on account of that departure, or not?

Here too, with the granting of success from God, glorified be He, you have reached the sound word on the matter. The truth of it is this: the greeting prayer is obligatory only within the mosque itself — not in its courtyard and not in its forecourt. If it is performed in those areas, that is good, since they have become part of the mosque and within its bounds. Therefore, if a person inside the mosque goes out to the courtyard and returns — as I have explained — he is not obliged to repeat it, because he has not yet gone out from the mosque's bounds.

The book *Tawil al-Sharia* records, relating it from the Prophet (ع), that he said:

> لَا تُقَامُ الْحُدُودُ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ، وَمَنْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ يُنْشِدُ ضَالَّتَهُ فِي مَسْجِدٍ فَقُولُوا: لا وجدت

The prescribed penalties are not to be carried out in the mosques; and whoever you hear calling out for his lost property in a mosque, say to him: May you not find it.

The same book records that the Prophet (ع) said:

> لَا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلَاةِ فِي مَرَابِضِ الْغَنَمِ

There is no harm in praying in the folds of sheep.

The author of *al-Majalis al-Mustansiriyya* — may the peace of God be upon its author — said in the eighth assembly: Hear now what we set before you concerning its meaning: prayer has seven ranks, by which the prayers of those who pray are graded one above another:

1. the prayer of the worshipper in his house, as a single prayer;
2. the prayer of the worshipper in the mosque of the market, as twelve prayers;
3. the prayer of the worshipper in the mosque of the tribe, as twenty-five prayers;
4. the prayer of the worshipper in the congregational mosque, as one hundred prayers;
5. the prayer of the worshipper in the Farthest Mosque, as one thousand prayers;
6. the prayer of the worshipper in the mosque of the Messenger of God, as ten thousand prayers;
7. the prayer of the worshipper in the Sacred House of God, as one hundred thousand prayers.

For every one of these there are abundant meanings and likenesses of wisdom.

Our lord, the Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his four hundred rules of conduct:

> الْجُلُوسُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ بَعْدَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ إِلَىٰ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ أَسْرَعُ لِطَلَبِ الرِّزْقِ مِنَ الضَّرْبِ فِي الْأَرْضِ

Sitting in the mosque from the breaking of dawn until the rising of the sun is swifter in bringing provision than traveling through the land.

And he said in it: The Muslim is not to spit toward the qibla; and if he does so forgetfully, let him ask forgiveness. And he said in it: A man is not to blow upon the place of his prostration, nor upon his food, nor upon his incense. And he said in it:

> ولا يصلي أحدكم وبين يديه سيف، فإن القبلة آمن

None of you is to pray with a sword before him, for the qibla is a place of safety.

And he said in it: Whoever eats any of the offensive foods, let him not come near the mosque.

edits.chapter_key: the shape of the prayer itself
edits.body_md:
I turn now to the characteristics of the prayer and its sunnahs.

In the question-and-answer book mentioned at the outset — arranged by one of its compilers according to the chapter order of *Daaim al-Islam* — the following exchange appears. Question: What do you say concerning what has come in the Book of Purity, that Ibn al-Kawwa repeatedly opposed Amir al-Muminin Ali (ع) by raising his voice during the prayer, and that Ali (ع) then recited:

> فَٱصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ

So be patient; the promise of God is true.

O our master, did Ali (ع) begin the prayer with the surah of which this verse is a part, or not? Answer: No. Rather, he recited this verse in order to silence him and to rebuke him.

Question: What do you say concerning what has come in the books of the Shariah regarding the long portions of al-mufassal, its middle portions, and its short portions? O our master, what are their limits in the madhhab of the Ahl al-Bayt (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ)? Answer: The long portions of al-mufassal run from al-Hujurat to al-Mujadila; its middle portions run from al-Mujadila to عَم يَتَسَآءَلُونَ; and its short portions run from عَم يَتَسَآءَلُونَ to al-Nas.

From the same source: whoever abandons the prayer without excuse, or abandons any of the prescribed works, has broken the covenant. Whoever accuses a believer, and the accused then swears by God, and the accuser does not believe him, has broken the covenant. Whoever commits fornication or kills a believer has broken the covenant. Whoever reviles the summoner, or reviles the one whom the summoner has appointed, has broken the covenant. If the summoner commands the believer to strive with his person and his wealth, and he refuses without excuse, he has broken the covenant. Whoever forms the intention for the prayer, and then that intention slips away before he enters the prayer — whether through preoccupation, forgetfulness, or anything else — and he then prays after that, his prayer does not suffice him.

It is not permissible for a man to recite within himself what he has not uttered with his tongue. Whoever performs the first tashahhud is not thereby excused from the second, though the second does suffice in place of the first.

He said in the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: whoever forms the intention for the prayer, and then that intention slips away before he enters it — whether through preoccupation, forgetfulness, or anything else — and he then prays after that, his prayer does not suffice him. And from the same book: the one praying makes the tawajjuh after the takbirat al-ihram, the imam and the follower being equal in this, so long as the imam has not preceded the follower in something; and he begins the recitation after the tawajjuh.

He said in *al-Ikhtisar*: he opens the prayer with a takbir in which he raises his hands, spreading his palms and joining his fingers in a straight extension. The least by which the prayer is completed — its minimum — is this:

1. Opening with the takbir
2. Standing, for whoever is able
3. Bowing
4. Prostration
5. Sitting for the tashahhud

Whoever performs these five limits, having forgotten or not knowing what lies beyond them, his prayer is complete. But whoever knows their limits and then deliberately omits something from the obligations or the sunnahs of the prayer has no prayer, and he must repeat what he omitted of the prayer in this way. As for the one who is ignorant of this, it is upon him to learn.

He said in *al-Akhbar*: the woman places her hands above her knees upon her thighs, so that she does not stoop too far and thereby raise her hindquarters.

He said in the book *Tawil al-Daaim*: those behind the imam, when he says:

> سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ

God has heard the one who praised Him.

say quietly:

> رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ

Our Lord, to You belongs all praise.

The exception is the one who relays for the imam when those praying behind him are many and one among them has been appointed to make them hear on his behalf. That man raises his voice with it and with the takbir, but he does not raise his voice with the tasbih.

He said in the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: whoever performs the first tashahhud is not thereby excused from the second, though the second suffices in place of the first. And he said in the book *Tawil al-Daaim*, concerning the outward sense, that when the one praying sits in the prayer he folds his left leg beneath him and keeps his right leg upright.

He said in the brief discourse on jurisprudence, whose questions come from the most eminent Shaykh Hasan ibn Mawla Adam al-Hindi and whose answers come from the sayyids of Yemen, may God sanctify all their souls: the prayer of a woman who has not undergone khafd is valid, and intimacy with her is permissible, and likewise for the man; but the sunnah is to hasten to that.

Our master and our lord Jafar ibn Sulayman, may God exalt his sanctity and grant us his intercession and his company, said in his noble epistle, which he entitled *al-Sayf al-Aqta fi Ibtal al-Bida*, with which he counseled his people and roused from heedlessness those among them whose sleep had grown long — the people of the island of Yemen — after he had settled among them and taken up residence there. Section: And of this also is what has been known and witnessed of many among you, men and women alike, who cling to the mountain of loyalty and come to the rope of obedience to God, glorified be He, by way of undertaking the obligation of the prayer, and yet their foreheads do not prostrate to God, glorified be He, in a single rakah of the prayer, so that the prayer is diminished of the rakahs that belong around it. This is among the gravest of all matters in its consequence, and the most notorious of them all in repute. Has there never reached the ears of such people the word of the Messenger of God (ع):

> بَيْنَ الْعَبْدِ وَبَيْنَ الْكُفْرِ تَرْكُ الصَّلَاةِ

and the word of Amir al-Muminin (ع):

> لَا حَظَّ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ لِمَنْ تَرَكَ الصَّلَاةَ

There is no portion in Islam for the one who abandons the prayer.

Given this — that one who abandons the prayer holds no share in Islam, and that abandoning the prayer is precisely what separates the servant from unbelief — no person who neglects the prayer should, while still counting himself among the faithful, suppose that he stands among the Muslims, or that he holds of Islam so much as the parings of a fingernail. God, glorified be He, has declared this in the verses of His clear Book:

> ومن يبتع غير الإسلام ديناً فلن يقبل منه وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.

Among the people of this description we have seen, those who abandon the prayer fall into two kinds:

- The first are people of tribal temper who have turned away from the concerns of religion altogether, people absorbed in themselves and removed from all of that — the animal nature dominant over them, as though they had sprung from the well.
- The second are people of arrogance and coarse insolence, the women among them most especially.

But there is no insolence and no arrogance against God, glorified be He, nor against His worship. Whoever takes that path has destroyed his own soul and wronged it. As for his Creator, glorified be He, He has no need of that person's worship. Its benefit returns only to the worshipper himself, and to those like him — the learned among them and the lowly. God did not create them and require their service in His worship except to benefit them by it, as God, glorified and exalted be He, has said:

> وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ

And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me.

There is no doubt that whoever walks that path has entered into the warning God, exalted be He, issues in the verses of His clear Book, where He says:

> إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِى سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ

Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell abased.

It was on that very path that Iblis met his end — and he is truly dead — for whenever a servant prostrates to his Lord, glorified be He, in his prayer, Iblis cries out: Woe to me, this one obeyed and I refused. As for the unbeliever, even though he does not pray the prayer of Islam or worship his Lord, glorified be He, with the worship that is accepted, he still has within his own religion a form of worship that he performs, handed down to him from his forebears. Not even the unbelievers of the lands of India are so arrogant toward the worship of God, glorified be He, nor do they turn away from Him with such turning away — men and women, the whole and the parts — except for those among them who fall under the two kinds already described and who follow them in their misguidance and deviation. Those two kinds are found in all the schools of Islam as well, and likewise in the creeds of every religion. But such conduct does not befit one who has attached himself to the walaya of the friends of God, glorified be He, by its firm mountain, and who traces himself, in his affairs, back to the people of piety and faith. No one has any claim of walaya to them except by holding fast to the hem of the prayer. Otherwise he is like one who proclaims upon himself, in the Hereafter, destruction and woe — like those who oppose the guiding call. Even if there are among them, men and women alike, some who are formed that way, leave them and what they are formed in, for they are not granted success in their affairs, while you, in your affairs, by the praise of God, glorified be He, are granted success. As for the one who acknowledges the call of the friend of God (ع), and the Garden and the Fire, the punishment and the reckoning, the balance and the path, the gathering and the raising — his reason requires him to hold fast to the worship of his Lord, glorified be He, through the prayer, which is the pillar of the religion and the support of Islam, and to comply through it with the command. He who warns has given excuse, and he who has cautioned against the punishment of his Lord has cleared himself. So let those who would set things right set their souls right by this, and whoever fears God and guards himself against Him — those are the ones who prosper.

He said in the book *Tawil al-Shariah*: The obligations of the prayer are seven:

1. The first takbir
2. The recitation
3. The bowing
4. The prostration
5. The tasbih
6. The greeting
7. The taslim

And he said in it: When you have made the takbir, it is not permissible for you to move your foot, to advance it or draw it back; rather you remain fixed. Nor may you speak from the opening takbir until the taslim, nor move from your place.

And he said in it: The Prophet (ع) said:

> أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَدَوَاتٍ

I have been commanded to prostrate upon seven members.

And he said in it: The Prophet (ع) said:

> لا تقرأ وأنت راكع ولا تحركوا الحصى في الصلاة ولا تلتفتوا التّغات الثعلب ولا تقعوا اقعاء القرد ولا تنقروا نقر الغراب

Do not recite while you are bowing; do not disturb the pebbles during the prayer; do not turn about as the fox turns; do not squat as the monkey squats; and do not peck as the crow pecks.

He said in it: He separates the two rakahs with a sitting. He said in it: Do not pray the obligatory prayer when the adhan is called — pray it when the iqama is given. He said in it: The Zuhr prayer is four rakahs. He said in it: It is related from the Prophet (ع) that he said:

> لَا تُطْرِقُوا فِي الرُّكُوعِ إِطْرَاقَ الْحِمَارِ وَالْكُبَابَهِ

Do not droop the head in the bowing with the drooping of the donkey and of the lowered beast.

He commanded, further, that the head not be dropped below the level of the back. He said in it: The head and the back are level and aligned in the prayer. He said in it: The Prophet (ع) said:

> مَنْ كَثُرَتْ صَلَاتُهُ بِاللَّيْلِ حَسُنَ وَجْهُهُ بِالنَّهَارِ

Whoever prays much by night, his face is made beautiful by day.

The author of the guarded epistle, which contains the protected secrets of the religion of God — the most eminent and noble Dai Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, may God exalt his sanctity and grant us his intercession and his company — said: The obligations of the prayer are seven, and they are:

1. The intention
2. The first takbir
3. The standing
4. The recitation
5. The bowing
6. The prostration
7. The taslim

He said in it: Five prayers have been appointed for every day. He said in it: The prayer has four limits, and they are:

1. The place
2. The time
3. The purity
4. The intention

He said in it: The five prayers are seventeen rakahs. He said in it: The prayer is of two kinds — obligation and sunnah. He said in it: For that reason Muhammad (ع) said:

> تَارِكُ سُنَّتِي مَلْعُونٌ

The one who abandons my sunnah is cursed.

Meaning: the one who abandons my legatee is one banished from the mercy of God. He said in it: The Messenger of God (ع) said:

> لَا صَلَاةَ لِمَنْ لَا يُؤَدِّي الزَّكَاةَ

There is no prayer for the one who does not pay the zakat.

He said in it: The movements of the prayer — the bowing and the prostration — are submission and humility. Then he said: For that reason the Messenger of God (ع) said:

> مَنْ لَمْ تَنْهَ صَلَاتُهُ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ لَمْ يَزْدَدْ مِنَ اللَّهِ اِلَّا بُعْدًا

Whoever is not restrained by his prayer from indecency and wrongdoing increases in nothing but distance from God.

And for that reason, the people of Shuayb said to him:

> يا شعيب أصلواتك تأمرك أن نترك ما يعبد آبائنا

O Shuayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped?

Then he said: it is because the outward prayer neither forbids nor commands.

Our master, the author of the *Majalis al-Mustansiriyya* — may the peace of God be upon its author — said in the sixth of these councils: You have heard what we recited to you of the divisions of the obligations of purity and its sunnahs, corresponding in number to the clauses of the shahada and its letters, since purity is one of the rights of the shahada. Among its rights also is the prayer. So listen now to what we recite to you of its meaning. The prayers are seven obligatory prayers and twelve sunnah prayers. The obligatory prayers are:

1. The prayer of residence, which is seventeen rakahs in every day and night
2. The prayer of travel, which is eleven rakahs in the day and night
3. The Friday prayer, which is not complete until four gather with the imam
4. The prayer of fear, part of which is prayed with the imam and the remainder of which is completed alone
5. The prayer of the circumambulation of the obligatory Hajj
6. The prayer of the circumambulation of the obligatory Umrah
7. The prayer over the bier, which is an obligation upon every Muslim who knows of it — until one of them undertakes it, whereupon the rest become volunteers in it

The sunnah prayers are:

1. The prayer of the Feast of the Breaking of the Fast
2. The prayer of the Feast of the Sacrifice
3. The prayer of the eclipse of the sun
4. The prayer of the eclipse of the moon
5. The prayer for rain
6. The prayer of the earthquake
7. The prayer for events that occur as signs
8. The prayer of the shaf and the witr
9. The prayer of the watira, which is two rakahs performed sitting
10. The prayer of the two rakahs of the dawn — for the Prophet (ع) made them up after the rising of the sun and made up the obligatory prayer after them
11. Twenty-eight rakahs in every day and night, among them:
    - The prayer of the oft-returning, which is six rakahs after the sun's decline
    - Eight rakahs between Zuhr and Asr
    - Ten rakahs between Maghrib and the later Isha
    - Four rakahs after the later Isha, which is the prayer of the night
12. The prayer of greeting the mosque upon entering it

Then he said, may the good pleasure of God be upon him, in the seventh of these councils: So listen now to what we recite to you — that in each of the five prayers there are seven obligations and twelve sunnahs. The seven obligations are:

1. The intention
2. Turning toward the qibla
3. Then the takbirat al-ihram
4. The recitation of the Opening of the Book
5. The bowing
6. The prostration
7. The sitting for the salutation

The twelve sunnahs are:

1. The adhan
2. The iqama
3. Saying, I have turned my face to Him who created the heavens and the earth, as one of pure faith, to the end of the words
4. Seeking refuge from the accursed Satan
5. Reciting a surah after the Opening of the Book in the first two rakahs of every obligatory prayer
6. Raising the hands at every rising from the bowing and every descent into it
7. The tasbih during the bowing
8. The imam's saying, God has heard the one who praised Him, and the follower's saying, Our Lord, to You belongs all praise
9. The tasbih during the prostration
10. The first sitting and the first tashahhud
11. The second tashahhud
12. Every prayer in which there is no first sitting has a qunut that stands in its place in the count, and every prayer in which there are two sittings for the tashahhud has no qunut in it

Our lord Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع) said in his Four Hundred Etiquettes:

> لَا يَجْمَعُ الْمُؤْمِنُ يَدَيْهِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُشْبِهُ بِأَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ

The believer does not clasp his hands together in the prayer while standing, resembling thereby the People of the Book.

And he said in it:

> إِذَا أَصَابَ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الصَّلَاةِ الدَّابَّةَ فَلْيَدْفِنْهَا أَوْ لِيَسْتُرْ عَلَيْهَا أَوْ لِيَضَعْهَا فِي ثَوْبِهِ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ

If any of you comes upon a crawling creature during the prayer, let him bury it, or cover it over, or place it in his garment until he has finished.

And he said in it:

> الْاِلْتِفَاتُ الْفَاحِشُ يَقْطَعُ الصَّلَاةَ فَمَنْ فَعَلَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ الْاِبْتِدَاءُ . اَلصَّلَاةُ بِالْأَذَانِ وَالْإِقَامَةِ وَالتَّكْبِيرِ

Gross turning about cuts off the prayer, and whoever does it must begin again: the prayer with the adhan, the iqama, and the takbir.

And he said in it:

> أَعْطُوا كُلَّ سُورَةٍ حَقَّهَا مِنَ الرُّكُوعِ وَالسُّجُودِ إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فِي الصَّلَاةِ

Give every surah its due of bowing and prostration when you are in the prayer.

And he said in it:

> أَجْلِسُوا بَيْنَ السَّجْدَتَيْنِ حَتَّى تَسْكُنَ جَوَارِحُكُمْ وَقُومُوا فَاِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ فِعْلِنَا

Sit between the two prostrations until your limbs are still, then rise — for that is our practice.

And he said in it:

> لِيَرْفَعِ السَّاجِدُ مُؤَخَّرَهُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ إِذَا سَجَدَ

Let the one who prostrates raise his haunches when he prostrates.

And he said in it:

> إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَاَسْمِعْ نَفْسَكَ الْقِرَاءَةَ وَالتَّسْبِيحَ وَالتَّكْبِيرَ وَإِذَا انْقَّلْتَ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ فَعَنْ يَمِينِكَ

When you pray alone, make yourself hear your recitation, your tasbih, and your takbir. When you turn away from the prayer, turn to your right.

A question was raised by the head of the island of India, Muhammad Ali ibn Salih al-Badri, may God preserve him, and answered by the lord and master, our master Hibat Allah, may God prolong his life. The following is its text and substance.

The second question: What does our master — may God perpetuate his support — say concerning a person who recites Surat al-Falaq and Surat al-Nas inadvertently in the obligatory prayer? Does he complete the prayer, or does he repeat it? And if it is permissible, what is the ruling for one who recited Surat al-Nas in the first rakah? Does he repeat it in the second, or does he recite the surah before it from its opening, or does he repeat the prayer? And if it is not permissible, what of one who recited Surat al-Ikhlas in the first rakah? Does he repeat it in the second, or does he recite the surah above it from its opening? May our master — may God perpetuate his exaltation — favor us with a satisfying answer.

Answer: We seek help from God for success and right direction, and from His friend and his full moon we ask for rain from the clouds of confirmation. No text has come from the friends of God forbidding the recitation of the two surahs of refuge in the obligatory prayer. So if the one praying recites them, his prayer is complete. If he recited Surat al-Nas in the first rakah, he repeats it in the last. Whoever recited Surat al-Ikhlas in the first recites al-Falaq in the second. One should not, however, deliberately recite in this manner in the obligatory prayer, placing it in the position of the sunnah.

edits.chapter_key: friday and the two festivals
edits.body_md:
### On the Friday Prayer

I turn now to the Friday prayer, and I set down first what I find in the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset — which one of its arrangers ordered according to the chapters of *Daaim al-Islam*.

The question: What do you say concerning what has come in the Book of Purity — that if three miles or more separate two congregational mosques, Friday prayer is established in each of them, whether they stand in one city or two; but if the distance between them in a single city falls short of that, Friday prayer is established in only one of them? Our master, if the distance is less than three miles and the two mosques belong to two separate cities, is Friday prayer established in both of them or not?

The answer: Friday prayer is not established in both when the distance between them is less than three miles, whether they belong to one city or to two.

The question concerns the words of our master al-Muayyad in the Friday sermon:

> فَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا مُتَعَمِّداً أَوْ مُسْتَخِفّاً بِحَقِّهَا مِنْ غَيْرِ عُذْرٍ لَهُ مَعَ إِمَامٍ عَدْلٍ أَوْ جَائِرٍ فَلَا تَجْمَعِ اللهُ شَمْلَهُ

Whoever abandons it deliberately, or makes light of its due, without excuse — whether under a just imam or an unjust one — may God not gather his affairs together; to the end of the passage.

The answer: It is not permissible to pray behind the people of injustice except for the sake of dissimulation, as has come in the Shariah from Mawlana al-Baqir Muhammad ibn Ali (ع), who said:

Do not count the prayer behind a الناصب or a الحروري as valid. Treat such a person as one of the pillars of المسجد and recite for yourself, as though you were praying alone.

> لَا تَعْتَدَّ بِالصَّلَاةِ خَلْفَ النَّاصِبِ وَلَا الْحَرُورِيِّ وَاجْعَلْهُ سَارِيَةً مِنْ سَوَارِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَاقْرَأْ لِنَفْسِكَ كَأَنَّكَ وَحْدَكَ

The commentary on the reports records that al-Husayn ibn Ali (ع) put the governor of Muawiya forward to lead the prayer over his brother al-Hasan ibn Ali (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ), and said:

> لَوْلَا السُّنَّةُ لَمَا قَدَّمْتُكَ

Were it not for the practice, I would not have put you forward.

By that, he meant the practice of the People of the House (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) in dissimulation — as one of the Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) said:

> التَّقِيَّةُ دِينِي وَدِينُ آبَائِي

Dissimulation is my religion and the religion of my fathers.

As for what is meant by "the unjust" in his words, it refers to whoever has been set up among the summoners and from whom injustice and transgression have appeared: it is obligatory to pray behind him, and it is incumbent upon the people, when they observe this in him, to bring the matter before the holder of authority and to await his response. This is the meaning of his saying:

> أَيُّهَا الصَّالِحُونَ فَتَحَقَّقُوا ذَلِكَ وَلَا تَرْتَابُوا بَعْدَ الْيَقِينِ فَقَدِ اعْتَصَمْتُمْ بِجَبَلِ اللَّهِ الْمَتِينِ

O righteous ones, verify this and do not fall into doubt after certainty, for you have taken firm hold of the strong mountain of God.

He says in the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: The Friday prayer behind the Imam of the Muslims is more excellent than the prayer behind his deputies. If the Imam is delayed because he is occupied with some of the interests of the Muslims, and his deputies pray in his stead in mosques that are near one another, then the prayer in his own mosque — the one in which it has been his custom to pray — is more fitting than in any other.

He says in it: The call to prayer that obliges the one upon whom the Friday duty rests to leave off buying and selling is the call given in the presence of the preacher when he sits in the place from which he delivers the sermon. If two of those obliged to the Friday prayer transact a sale at the time when it is forbidden, their sale is not annulled. Whoever grows thirsty while the Imam is on the pulpit may drink.

He says in it: If the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday and his state of purity is broken, he descends and performs the ablution; then if he wishes he repeats the sermon, and if he wishes he prays — all of this suffices him. If he delivers the sermon seated because of an ailment, that suffices him. It is disliked for him to omit the sitting between the two sermons, but if he has done so, repetition is not obligatory upon him.

If the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday and then some matter overtakes the people and they go off to it, and only one man remains with him, then he prays four cycles. If he has delivered the sermon to the people on Friday and prayed one cycle with them and then they all departed and he remained alone, he prays the Friday prayer as two cycles. If he has opened the prayer and they departed before he bowed, he begins afresh the noon prayer of four cycles. If the Imam prays the Friday prayer with the people, and when he has finished the second cycle he rises to stand and then remembers, it is upon him to sit, to make the testimony, to give the greeting of peace, and to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

And from it: Whoever among the people of Friday sleeps while waiting for the Friday prayer, and the prayer is established and purification is not possible for him, performs the dry ablution and prays with the Imam, then repeats it as four.

He says in the book of reports: And he leans upon his sword; if he does not find a sword, then upon a staff.

He says in the book *Tawil al-Shariah*: The sermon is before the prayer, and the prayer after the sermon is two cycles. He divides the sermon into two portions with a sitting that separates them. The raising of the voice in its recitation distinguishes it from the noon prayer on the remaining days, and the noon prayer is at seven hours. He said: The call to stand for prayer comes after the sermon.

He says in it: The practice of the respondents in the assembly of the summoner is like the practice of the congregation on Friday, or the congregation behind the Imam. When the preacher on Friday ascends the pulpit and faces the people, silence becomes obligatory, such that it is not permissible for anyone to speak or to occupy himself with anything other than listening to him and giving ear to him.

He says in it: It is not permissible for him to give suck unless his summoner has appointed him to the suckling and chosen him for it. When the Imam recites, listening becomes obligatory and nothing else, and it is not permissible to turn away from him. Likewise, it is not permissible for the respondent to press proposals upon the summoner or to demand from him the various branches of knowledge, for he knows better how to raise his children.

Our master Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said in his *Hidden Epistle*: The Friday prayer points to Muhammad (ع), who is the gate of the Garden, and he has two summonses — an outward summons to the outward face of his Shariah and an inward summons to the interpretation of his law. Then he said: Because the prayer on the remaining days was four cycles, on Friday it became two, and the sermon was made a substitute for the two cycles. It is praise, admonition, supplication, and exposition from the Lord of exposition, and it is never without warning. The sitting during the sermon is the separation between the upper light and the lower light; the Qaim (ع) rises with the two lights. Then he said: The preacher is not to deliver the sermon upon the call to prayer that has already been given, until the muezzin who stands before the seat gives the call after the Imam has ascended the pulpit. Then he said: The call is given only in the congregational mosque, as an announcement. Then he said: Whoever gives the call on that day in one of the mosques other than the congregational mosque has erred, and if he did it deliberately he is punished and commanded to perform the washing of Friday. Then he said:

> فَاعْرِفْ فَضْلَ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ حَتَّىٰ يَجْمَعَ اللَّهُ شَمْلَكَ بِيَوْمِ السَّبْتِ فَتَسْتَرِيحَ وَتَسْبُتَ وَلَا تَشْقَىٰ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ

Know the excellence of the day of Friday, so that God may gather your affairs together on the day of the Sabbath and you may rest and repose, spared from wretchedness — if God the Exalted wills.

Mawlana Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع) said in his Four Hundred Points of Conduct:

> مَنْ كَانَتْ لَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ حَاجَةٌ فَلْيَطْلُبْهَا فِي ثَلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ: ١- فِي يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ سَاعَةَ زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ ٢- وَحِينَ تَهبُّ الرِّيَاحُ وَتُفْتَحُ أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ وَتَنْزِلُ الرَّحْمَةُ ٣- وَسَاعَةً فِي آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ عِنْدَ طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ.

> وَإِنَّ مَلَكَيْنِ يُنَادِيَانِ هَلْ مِنْ تَائِبٍ فَيُتَابَ عَلَيْهِ هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ فَيُعْطَىٰ هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ فَيُغْفَرَ لَهُ هَلْ مِنْ طَالِبِ حَاجَةٍ فَأَجِيبُوا دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ
>
> "Two angels call out: Is there anyone repenting, that his repentance be accepted? Is there anyone asking, that he be given? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that he be forgiven? Is there anyone with a need? So answer the summoner of God."

Whoever has a need before God, let him seek it in three hours:

1. On the day of Friday, at the hour when the sun passes its zenith.
2. When the winds blow, and the gates of heaven are opened, and mercy descends.
3. An hour at the end of the night, at the breaking of dawn.

He says in it: the supplication of devotion in the Friday prayer falls before the bowing in the second cycle. The recitation on Friday is: in the first cycle, the chapter of the Congregation after the Opening of the Book, and in the second, the Opening of the Book followed by the chapter of the Hypocrites.

He says in it, among legal questions that are all marvels, another question: What do you say of a preacher who was delivering the sermon on Friday when a man entered through the door of the congregational mosque, whereupon the sermon of that preacher was spoiled, and so was the prayer of those who prayed with him? The answer: that preacher is the property of the man who entered through the door of the congregational mosque, for that man had appointed him as his deputy; so when he came in upon him, it was no longer permissible for him to go before his master, nor to lead him in prayer.

### On the Prayer of the Two Festivals

I likewise set down here what is contained in the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset, arranged according to the order of the chapters of the book *Daaim al-Islam*.

The question: What do you say concerning what has come in the Shariah — that no tashriq is incumbent upon the traveler except in a congregational city? Our master, is what is intended by tashriq here the festival prayer, or not? And whoever forgets one of the magnifications in the festival prayer, or more than one — how should he act?

The answer: It has come in the book *al-Mujzi*, in the section on the ages of camels, cattle, and the like, that there is no tashriq except in a congregational city — that is, no prayer of the two festivals — because the two festival prayers are prayed at the rising of the sun, and the one who prays them is called المشرّق (al-mushriq). And it has come in *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: whoever forgets part of the magnification completes it before he bows; and if he has already passed beyond the bowing and is certain of the omission, he performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

The question: What do you say concerning the magnification from the day of Arafah to the last of the days of tashriq being twenty-three magnifications, while in our lands they add one magnification after the festival prayer so that it becomes twenty-four? And what is the meaning of this?

The answer: The magnification in those days is twenty-three, and it is a likeness of what obtains in the summons of the five speakers — the possessors of firm resolve — who correspond to the five prayers, drawn from the mention of the ten spiritual ranks and the ten bodily ranks, and the mention of the speaker of the cycle, his executor, and the Imam of the age.

> فَخُذْ مَا أُوتِيتَ وَكُنْ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ

So take what you have been given, and be among the thankful.

From another source: whoever prays the festival prayer while owing a makeup of the dawn prayer, his festival prayer is valid and he does not repeat it; and likewise the funeral prayer.

From our master al-Hasan ibn Idris: whoever prays the festival prayer before bringing out the alms of the breaking of the fast does not repeat it, and he hands over the alms afterward. The washing for the two festivals is a practice of the Prophet. The first of its time is the breaking of dawn, and the last of it is the time of the sun's passing the zenith. Whoever prays the festival prayer before the sun passes the zenith, for an excuse, it is valid for him.

He says in the book *Mukhtasar al-Musannaf*: the washing for the two festivals is a practice of the Prophet; the first of its time is the breaking of dawn and the last of it is the time of the sun's passing the zenith.

He says in the book of reports: and the supplication of devotion is:

> اَللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَعَافِنِي وَاعْفُ عَنِّي فِي الدِّينِ وَالدُّنْيَا إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

O God, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me well-being, and pardon me in religion and in the world. You are powerful over all things.

He says in it: if the people of the desert attend — and those travelers who choose to attend the festival — that is good, and there is merit in it for them. And from it: it is fitting for whoever is among the people of the desert, at two leagues from the city or less, to witness the festival.

He says in it: its congregation is five, one of them the Imam, as with the congregation of the Friday prayer; and where there is one who establishes it, it is an obligation like the obligation of Friday. Whoever misses it with the one who establishes it but catches the two sermons prays it as four as well. Whoever misses one cycle of the festival prayer and catches the second with the Imam adds to it another cycle with its magnifications. The practice regarding the magnification is that it begins after the completion of the fast, on the night of the breaking of the fast and on the day of the breaking of the fast, until he prays and finishes the prayer. Whoever prays the festival prayer raises his hands with every magnification. Whoever forgets part of the magnification completes it before he bows; and if he has passed beyond the bowing and is certain of the omission, he performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

He says in the book *al-Musannaf*: the festival prayer is not prayed at Mina. Likewise our master al-Qadi al-Numan ibn Muhammad said in *Tawil al-Daaim*; and it has been verified from our master Idris ibn Hasan that the festival prayer is not prayed there in congregation, but each one prays it by himself, one by one.

He says in the book of questions and answers mentioned at the outset: intercourse with one's wife is permitted on the night of the festival of the breaking of the fast and before the festival prayer.

Our master Jafar ibn Mansur al-Yaman said in the book *al-Rida al-Batin*: it is permitted after the festival of the breaking of the fast to fast on the following day and thereafter. And he says in it: it is not permitted after this festival — meaning the festival of the sacrifice — as it is permitted after the festival of the breaking of the fast.

Our master Zayd ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said in the *Hidden Epistle*, concerning the prayer of the festival of the breaking of the fast: الفطر (al-fitr) in the language means appearance and beginning. One says تَفَطَّرَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَانْفَطَرَتْ (تَفَطَّرَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَانْفَطَرَتْ) — meaning the earth split open and what lay within it appeared and came forth. Likewise تَفَطَّرَتِ الشَّجَرَةُ (tafattarat al-shajarah) means that its hidden fruit appeared. And فَطَرَ نَابُ الْبَعِيرِ (fatara nab al-bair) means that it came up and appeared. In all these examples there runs a single sense: it is the day on which the command and the things that had been hidden come to light. From this, the breaking of the fast was named fitr, for fasting is silence and concealment. God the Exalted said in the story of Maryam:

> إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًۭا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّۭا

I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, so I shall not speak to any human being today.

That is: I have vowed silence and stillness, showing nothing of what is within me. So fitr is the appearance of secrets and the knowledge of hidden things. And His saying,

> وإذا السماء انفطرت

And when the sky is split open,

means that it was cleft and what was within it came forth. In another meaning, الْفِطْر is the new; and فَطَرَ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ (fatara Allah al-khalq) means the beginning of His fashioning of them. The day of the breaking of the fast is therefore the day of the manifestation of the command that had been veiled. Then he said: Whoever has fasted the days of the month of Ramadan, for him is the breaking of the fast, the festival, and joy; and whoever does not know the meaning of the reality of fasting and its limits has nothing of God, and he is as God, mighty and majestic, said:

> عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ تَصْلَى نَارًا حَامِيَةً

Toiling, weary, burning in a scorching fire.

The festival prayer has neither a call to prayer nor a call to stand. He then said: the sermon at the breaking of the fast comes after the prayer. He said: the recitation in it is aloud. He said: the prayer of the sacrifice is on the day of the sacrifice — the day of the pilgrimage. He then said: the fact that this sermon begins contrary to all other sermons is a sign that the command appears otherwise than it was in the cycles that have passed. Every sermon begins with praise, except the sermon of the day of the sacrifice, which begins with the four magnifications.

edits.chapter_key: eclipse, fear, rain, and the night vigil
edits.body_md:
I turn now to the prayer of the eclipse. What follows is drawn from the book of questions and answers mentioned earlier, which one of its arrangers organized according to the chapters of كِتَابُ دَعَائِمِ الْإِسْلَامِ (The Pillars of Islam).

**Question:** Concerning the eclipse that occurred in the year eight hundred and thirty-seven, in the month of Dhu al-Qadah: it began on Monday, two hours after the sun had passed its height, and the solar eclipse fell out in accordance with the reckoning of the table. Yet the letters of the Brethren of Purity, in the treatise on astronomy, state that a solar eclipse occurs only at the end of the month, and the cause of this is given there. This has happened repeatedly in years before this one. We were fasting during the first days of the blessed month of Ramadan when an eclipse occurred, and the believers were left perplexed about how the matter is to be answered.

**Answer:** A statement has come from Mawlana, the author of the letters (ع), in summary, and the pure Imams and the ranks that follow them have explained it. They said that the eclipse of the moon occurs at the dawn of the fifteenth and at the dawn of the sixteenth, while the eclipse of the sun may occur at the beginning of the month or at its end. The matter is in the hand of God.

> وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ

There is no might and no power except with God, the Most High, the Great.

**Question:** One who joins the imam at the third rakah counts it as the beginning of his own prayer. He bows with the imam's bowing and prostrates with his prostration. When the imam rises from the prostration, he rises with him and prays the five bowings with him and prostrates with him. When the imam makes the testimony, the latecomer sits poised and ready. When the imam gives the salutation, the latecomer rises and completes what remains upon him of the bowings; he recites the qunut, bows, prostrates, makes the testimony, and gives the salutation. He does not count the first two prostrations he performed with the imam, just as is done by one who catches only the prostration at the end of the obligatory prayers with the imam.

Another case: whoever misses the eclipse prayer with the imam counts his joining as the beginning of his own prayer. If he comes before the first two prostrations, he prays what remains with the imam, and whenever the imam prostrates in the first two prostrations, he prostrates with him — for it has been mentioned that one who leaves these is counted as unable. When the imam rises, the latecomer prays the five bowings with him and prostrates and rises with the imam; when the imam prostrates, he prostrates with him; when the imam sits, the latecomer sits poised and ready; and when the imam gives the salutation, the latecomer rises and prays what remains upon him of the bowings, then prostrates, makes the testimony, and gives the salutation. He does not count the first two prostrations in which he prostrated with the imam, just as is done by one who has been outstripped in the prayer and catches only the prostration and the obligatory portions.

It is said in the book of purity: the eclipse prayer is not to be prayed until the eclipse appears and is seen. It is not prayed on the word of an astrologer or of anyone else that it is occurring, and if a veil of cloud or anything else intervenes, it is not prayed until the eclipse appears and is seen with the eye.

I turn now to the prayer of fear, and again from that same book of questions and answers.

**Question:** What do you say concerning what has come in the book of purity — that when there is the crossing of swords, close fighting, and the thrusting of spears, they make their prayers into takbir, so that they say one takbir in the place of each bowing? O our master, do they shorten the takbir as they shorten in the prayer of fear? **Answer:** He shortens in the takbir as shortening has been made obligatory in it.

It is said in the book مُخْتَصَرُ الْمُصَنَّفِ: if the imam prays the prayer of fear with three men while three men stand guard for him, that is permitted. If their number is fewer than three, it is not recommended for them to pray the prayer of fear, since the word "party" does not apply to fewer than three. And if the eclipse prayer and a funeral prayer come together for the imam along with fear, he prays over the funeral, and prays the eclipse prayer and the prayer of fear.

I turn now to the prayer for rain. It is said in كِتَابُ الْاِقْتِصَارِ, and in الأخبار, and in اَلْمُنْتَخَبَةُ: then he faced the people and said one hundred takbirs; then he turned to his right and glorified God one hundred times; then he turned to his left and declared the oneness of God one hundred times, raising his voice in all of this. Then he faced the people and praised God with one hundred utterances of praise and magnification, and extolled Him. It is said in the book of purity: he delivered two sermons in the same manner as is done for the two feasts; then he descended and departed, and the people departed. He delivers the sermon leaning upon an Arabian bow, if he finds one, as the Messenger of God (ع) did. And from the same source: if they go out on a day other than Monday, there is no harm in it. It is said in مُخْتَصَرُ الْمُصَنَّفِ: whoever delivers the sermon before the prayer must pray and then deliver the sermon.

I turn now to the witr prayer, the two bowings of dawn, and the qunut, and again from that book of questions and answers.

**Question:** Concerning a man who is heedless of the qunut. **Answer:** In the witr he must repeat, and in the dawn prayer he performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness.

**Question:** What do you say concerning a man who prays the witr and forgets the qunut, then remembers it after he has bowed or prostrated or sat? Does he repeat the witr, or does he perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness? **Answer:** The qunut is a supplication that is not to be abandoned deliberately. Whoever forgets it need not repeat, and there are no two prostrations of forgetfulness in the sunnah prayers. Whoever abandons it in the witr deliberately must repeat. The least of the qunut is three glorifications or three takbirs.

**Question:** When is the qunut recited in the witr? **Answer:** The qunut is recited after the worshipper says:

> رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ

Our Lord, to You belongs all praise.

Let that be verified. And whoever prays the shaf prayer of two bowings and then occupies himself with something until dawn breaks repeats the shaf as a make-up. If he has prayed three bowings and only the sitting remains until dawn breaks, he does not repeat the three, but makes up the sitting with the intention of a make-up.

**Question:** Concerning the worshipper who gives the salutation after the first bowing of the witr — is speech permitted to him, or does he join the consecration to the consecration? For it has been said that the prayer of one seated is half the prayer of one standing, and it has been said in another place:

> أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَحْرِيمُهَا تَكْبِيرُهَا وَتَحْلِيلُهَا تَسْلِيمُهَا

الصَّلَاةُ تَحْرِيمُهَا التَّكْبِيرُ وَتَحْلِيلُهَا التَّسْلِيمُ — the prayer: its consecration is its takbir, and its release is its salutation. By which of the two, then, does one act? Answer: our master the Judge al-Numan, may God raise his sanctity, has mentioned in اَلْمُنْتَخَبَةُ أَنْ:

> وَالْوِتْرُ قَدْ يُفْصَلُ بِالسَّلَامِ
> مِنْ غَيْرِ أَعْمَالٍ وَلَا كَلَامٍ

The witr may be divided by the salutation, without actions and without speech. And if one is compelled to speak, there is no harm in it so long as the talk is not prolonged.

**Question:** Is it permissible to perform the shaf and the witr in their proper time during the first dawn — which the Arabs call ذَنَبُ السِّرْحَانِ — before the second dawn spreads across the sky, or not? And does the dispensation extend to praying the two bowings of the sunnah of dawn? **Answer:** The shaf prayer and the witr are performed in their proper time so long as the dawn has not spread; this is established.

Whoever prays the dawn prayer with the imam and bows before the imam, then raises his head and bows a second time with the imam, his prayer is valid, because his prayer follows the prayer of the imam. But if he prayed alone, he repeats the prayer. Whoever prays the witr and forgets the qunut performs the two prostrations of forgetfulness after the salutation.

**Question:** If a man prays the shaf, then enters the mosque and prays the greeting of the mosque during the time of the shaf, does he repeat the shaf or not? **Answer:** He repeats the shaf, because it is not for him to pray after it until dawn breaks. When dawn has broken he prays the greeting, then prays the dawn prayer.

It is said in مَعَالِمُ الدِّينِ: the witr prayer is obligatory, and there is no dispensation in abandoning it; it is among the appendages of the obligatory prayers, even though it is a sunnah.

It is said in the book of purity: he recites in the first bowing the opening of the Book and the surah:

> قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ
>
> "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak."

In the second bowing, I recite the opening of the Book and the surah:

> قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ

Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.

I then make the testimony and give the salutation. These two bowings are part of the witr. I sit cross-legged throughout both of them, as already described, spreading my palms upon my thighs with my fingertips upon my knees, and I recite. When I have finished the recitation, I bow and place the inner surfaces of my palms upon my knees, still seated cross-legged. When I raise my head from the bowing, I draw my right foot back behind me, set my feet upright, prostrate, and then sit for the testimony as one sits in prayer.

Our master Muhammad ibn Fahd, may God raise his sanctity, said in his noble treatise, which he named لَاحِبَةُ سَبِيلِ الْهُدَى لِلْمُهْتَدِينَ, in the twenty-second question: you also asked about one who prays the shaf and the witr, then sits afterward for as long as is easy for him, then rises and prays the dawn — its sunnah and its obligation — and it afterward becomes clear to him that he was still in the night and the dawn had not yet come. What is his condition in that prayer? The answer is that his shaf and his witr stand confirmed, and he must repeat the dawn, both its sunnah and its obligation, unless the dawn was close upon him, in which case the sunnah prayer also stands confirmed for him. This is because it has come in the books of the friends of God (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) that it is permissible to pray it before dawn, on account of the noble meaning beneath this that permits it. So know this.

The Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (ع), said in his four hundred points of conduct:

> تَوَكَّلُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ عِنْدَ رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ بَعْدَ فَرَاغِكُمْ مِنْهَا فَفِيهَا تُعْطَى الرَّغَايِبُ

Place your trust in God at the two bowings of dawn after you have finished them, for in them the things most desired are granted.

Our master and Mawlana Sharaf al-Din Jafar, son of our master Sulayman — may God raise their sanctity in the chambers of the Garden — set down in his book الْحَدَائِقُ الْأَنِيقَةُ النَّفْسَانِيَّةُ الْمُشْتَمِلَةُ عَلَى الْجَوَابَاتِ الْبُرْهَانِيَّةِ, drawing from the answers of our master Daud ibn 'Ajab to his son in religion, Sulayman ibn Hasan, the following of his chosen words: as for your question about one who owes a make-up of the witr — is it permissible for him to pray voluntary prayers or not — and about one who owes a make-up of the sunnah prayers: it is permissible, though it is better that he give precedence to the witr make-up before everything else.

I turn now to the sunnah and the voluntary prayers, again from that book of questions and answers.

Question: What do you say concerning the prayer of opening, the prayer of glorification, and the prayer of night vigil? Has anything fixed come down regarding their recitation, and what ought to be recited in them of the surahs?

Answer: Nothing fixed has come down. They are like the sunnah and voluntary prayers: one recites in them whatever one wishes.

Question: What do you say concerning the witr prayer and the prayer of the two feasts? Is it permissible for one who has not memorized the appointed portion of the Quran to recite something else in them?

Answer: If he has not memorized it, he recites what is easy for him and does not abandon the prayer.

Question: What do you say concerning the supplications of the night vigil? Is it permissible for one who has not memorized them to intend a voluntary prayer?

Answer: He intends the prayer of the night vigil and supplicates with the supplication if he has memorized it; otherwise he supplicates with what is easy for him, while still intending the prayer of the night vigil. It is twelve bowings, and it has two times: one is between the sunset prayer and the evening prayer, in which a person prays using the short surahs of the detailed portion.

Question: What do you say concerning the tarawih prayer, when the believers pray behind the imam for the sake of protective concealment with the intention of a voluntary prayer, while the imam recites the Quran from its beginning to its end — a practice not followed in the obligatory prayers, and particularly not in the witr, the sunnah of dawn, and the greeting of the mosque?

Answer: There is no harm in it for the sake of protective concealment, but they do not follow him as a leader.

Question: It is mentioned in كِتَابُ الشَّوَاهِدِ وَالْبَيَانِ that the worshipper prays the noon prayer as ten bowings, the afternoon prayer as eight bowings, the sunset prayer as five bowings, and the evening prayer as ten bowings.

Answer: The reliance is upon الدعائم, which is the gathering place of the questions. If a person leaves anything of the sunnah for the sake of protective concealment, he makes it up.

Question: It has come down concerning the prayer of glorification that when he rises from the second prostration he glorifies ten times. O our master, how does he do this — seated upon his feet, or standing?

Answer: When one who prays the prayer of glorification wishes to do this, he sits poised and ready after raising his head from the second prostration, glorifies ten times, then rises for the second bowing. Likewise, after the second bowing, he sits poised and ready after the second prostration, glorifies ten times, then sits settled, makes the testimony, and gives the salutation. He does the same in the last two bowings. This practice, however, is irregular. As for that upon which practice rests in the prayer of glorification: he sits settled after raising his head from the second prostration in each bowing and glorifies ten times, then rises for the next — or, after the second, makes the testimony following the glorification, remaining settled in his sitting during both the glorification and the testimony.

Question: It has come down concerning the prayer of sufficiency that in the first bowing one recites the opening of the Book, the chapter of sincerity, the chapter of the disbelievers, and the verse of the Throne — once each; in the second, twice each; in the third, three times each; and in the fourth, four times each. O our master, does he repeat the opening of the Book in each bowing, or is it recited once in each bowing? Kindly give the answer.

Answer: He recites the opening of the Book once in each bowing, and God knows best.

It is said in مُخْتَصَرُ الْآثَارِ: whoever has not learned the Quran, let him recite what is easy of it. God, Exalted is He, said:

> فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْآنِ

So recite what is easy of the Quran.

And whoever wishes may stand the whole night with a single surah, repeating it, or with part of a surah, or with two surahs or more than that.

It is said in تَأْوِيلُ الدَّعَائِمِ, concerning the voluntary prayer of the Messenger of God (ع) upon his mount while he was making his way toward Medina: he would gesture with his head in indication of the prostration, with the direction of prayer behind him.

It is said in the abridged discourse on jurisprudence — whose questions are from the most honorable Shaykh Hasan, son of the Mawla Adam al-Hindi, and whose answers are from the masters of Yemen, may God sanctify all their spirits — that whoever prays between the obligation of the later evening prayer and its voluntary prayer whatever he wishes, then prays the voluntary prayer, does not intend it as a make-up, for it is called the prayer of the night.

Our master and Mawlana Jafar, son of our master Sulayman, may God raise their sanctity in the Gardens, wrote in like manner to his servant, the compiler of this book, from the island of Yemen to the island of Hind, concerning the matter of the prayer of Umm Daud, which is known among all who are of the ranks. He had asked him about it so that the sources and the paths might be made clear by his sufficient answer. He mentioned what concerns the prayer of Umm Daud and the supplication of opening, and that Qasim ibn Fir — the summoner of the maimed and blinded Daudi faction — commanded his companions to pray it, to fast it, and to supplicate with it in the month of Rabi al-Awwal of the year 1042, when the fifteenth of it fell on a Friday and they were in prison, and likewise in the honored month of Ramadan of that year. You asked about that, and about its permissibility and its practice, and I answered the one who asked you about it that Mawlana al-Sadiq (ع) gave no text on the aforementioned prayer of Umm Daud except for the month of Rajab, and he commanded her to purify herself. And when I asked him about it, and whether that supplication may be recited in a month other than Rajab, he said:

> فِي يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ وَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمَ جُمُعَةٍ لَمْ يَفْرُغْ صَاحِبُهُ اِلَّا وَقَدْ غُفِرَ لَهُ

On the day of 'Arafah; and if it falls on a Friday, the one who performs it does not finish until he has been forgiven.

The matter stands as I have stated it. Nothing outward exists without a sign by which it is recognized, and no practice is valid without a supporting text. In the command given to Umm Daud — to seek forgiveness until the month of Rajab, along with the supplication of opening already mentioned — there is both sufficiency and satisfaction. And in the text that follows, specifying the day of 'Arafah when it is not a Friday, and when it is a Friday as he mentioned, there is likewise sufficiency and satisfaction: the practice applies only to that specified day. As for any occasion other than these, no one should proceed without a text. If a text exists in the matter, let it be followed; and if not, then little practice, as the Prophet (ع) said:

> عَمَلٌ قَلِيلٌ فِي سُنَّةٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عَمَلٍ كَثِيرٍ فِي بِدْعَةٍ

You asked whether, on the day of 'Arafah, one should supplicate with the mentioned supplication or perform the mentioned prayer on that day. The root of the matter is that the mentioned supplication has as its condition the mentioned prayer, for he said:

> فَأَيْنَ أَنْتَ مِنْ دُعَاءِ الْاِسْتِفْتَاحِ

Where are you with regard to the supplication of opening?

When I asked him about it, he made it known to her by that mentioned prayer, then by the mentioned supplication. So if you pray on that day, its prayer is upon that; and if one supplicates with it on that day, it is accepted for its excellence and its nobility. God knows best and judges best; from His friends we learn in order to know, and God grants success to what is right and guides to the best of means.

In the questions from some of the shaykhs of Hind (رض), with answers from some of our masters — the summoners of Yemen, may God raise their sanctity — it is said:

Question: Most of the believers do not keep the sunnah fasts as they pray the sunnah prayers.

Answer: It is permissible for them to omit the sunnah fast, and no make-up is required of them. As for the sunnah prayer, whoever has missed it ought to make it up. The Imams (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ) and their followers did so, and they have reward from God if they fast.

Our master and Mawlana Hibat Allah, son of our master Ibrahim, said in his answer to questions from his servant and the humblest of his slaves, Salih ibn Ahmad — answering him from the island of Yemen to the island of Hind in the year 1135: You asked concerning what has come in the books, that the prophets — such as Jesus and others — and the Imams, such as Mawlana 'Ali and Mawlana Zayn al-Abidin and others among the Imams, the blessings of God be upon them all, at the time of a great event would call for water, perform the ablution, and pray two bowings, and in some instances four bowings, for the relief of distress. It has not been made clear at what time they prayed. Is that prayer to be prayed at all times of trial, affliction, and calamity, or only at a time when the sunnah and voluntary prayers are permitted? May the master and owner graciously give the answer.

Answer: By the help of God, Exalted is He, and the favor of His friend upon His earth (ع), and by the instruction of my master Badr al-Din, the inspired and the helper: the prayer of the prophets and the prayer of the Imams, the blessings and peace and benedictions of God be upon them all, flows down to us from them at times of grave matters and events, and at the descent of calamities and disasters. Their prayer is praise of God and thanksgiving for what He disclosed to them of the secret of affairs, and for their knowledge that those things do not come to pass except by a measure decreed. You mentioned that they, the blessings of God be upon them, did not inform us at what times it is to be prayed, but only reported it in a summary way. Yes, it is permissible to pray it at all the times when the sunnah and voluntary prayers are permitted; prohibition has come only concerning the forbidden times, which are not hidden from one of clear mind and illumined form. When their servants and their followers wish to pray that mentioned prayer, and by it to repel all calamities and to be shielded by it from all evils and ruinous things, it is for them to be guided by their guidance and to follow their practice. May God, Mighty and Majestic, keep us firm upon obedience to them, grant us their accepted intercession, and supply us from their secret and their blessings. He is the Guardian of that and the One able to do it, by the right that is His and the secret that is with Him.

I turn now to the prostration of the Quran, and again from that book of questions and answers.

Question: What do you say concerning one who recites a supplication in which there is a verse of prostration? Is it obligatory upon him to prostrate or not?

Answer: If it is among the binding ones, he must prostrate.
